'''Yoshie Katsurada''' ({{langx|ja|桂田 芳枝}}, 3 September 1911 – 10 May 1980){{r|hokudai|nams}} was a Japanese mathematician specializing in [[differential geometry]].{{r|kobayashi}} She became the first Japanese woman to earn a doctorate in mathematics, in 1950, and the first to obtain an imperial university professorship in mathematics, in 1967.{{r|frederic}}

==Life==
Katsurada was born in [[Akaigawa, Hokkaido]] on 3 September 1911, a daughter of an elementary school principal. In high school in [[Otaru]], she took special instruction in mathematics from a boys' mathematics instructor. Graduating from high school in 1929, she began auditing classes at the {{ill|Tokyo Physics School|ja|東京物理学校}}, a predecessor to the [[Tokyo University of Science]], in 1931.{{r|hokudai}}

She began working as an administrative assistant in the [[Hokkaido University]] Department of Mathematics in 1936. In 1938 she began study in mathematics at [[Tokyo Woman's Christian University]], withdrawing in 1940 to transfer to Hokkaido University. She graduated from Hokkaido University in 1942, and in the same year became an assistant professor there.{{r|hokudai}}

In 1950, she completed a doctorate in mathematics at Hokkaido University, under the supervision of Shoji Kawaguchi,{{r|hokudai}} becoming the first Japanese woman to earn a doctorate in mathematics,{{r|hokudai|frederic}} and earning a promotion to associate professor.{{r|hokudai}} She remained at Hokkaido University for the remainder of her career, with research visits to [[Sapienza University of Rome]], [[ETH Zurich]], and the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. She was promoted to full professor in 1967, the first female professor in mathematics at a former imperial university.{{r|hokudai}}

She retired in 1975,{{r|hokudai}} and died on 10 May 1980.{{r|nams}}

==Research==
Katsurada's early research, from the beginning of her studies into the mid-1950s, primarily concerned [[line element]]s; this was the primary interest of her advisor Shoji Kawaguchi, with whom she continued to collaborate on this subject. After visiting [[Heinz Hopf]] at [[ETH Zurich]] in 1957–1958, she shifted interests to [[submanifold]]s and [[hypersurface]]s in [[Riemannian manifold]]s, publishing well-regarded work in this area.{{r|kobayashi}}

==Recognition==
Several papers in the 1972 volume of the ''Hokkaido Mathematical Journal'' are dedicated to Katsurada in honor of her 60th birthday. Katsurada was given the Hokkaido Culture Award in 1973.{{r|hokudai}}
